utterances.text: Yes, there is a higher chance of that, and indeed if I remember the reporting right, one of the rounds was thought to have hit something on its entry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I have a last question for you. The 170 degree for the one which was hitting the Markale market and four others at 220 and 240 degrees, it was said there was an anomaly. Therefore, number five must have been fired from 220 to 240 as well. We saw that in one of the reports. Now, what is the anomaly apart from that it's a different outcome of a measurement? What other reasons were there not to accept the 170 degrees and say being an anomaly compared to the others we make it 220 and 240?

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- it -- it was the -- if I remember correctly from the reporting, it -- it was a re-examination of the fuse furrows and the evidence that it had hit the side of a building or an edge of a roof or something on entry that had affected the line of that particular crater, if I remember the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that if it had hit something else and had ricochetted from there, that it is very difficult then to say from which direction it exactly came before it ricochetted and then ended up at a certain spot.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be that much more difficult, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no further questions for you. I think we have dealt with these pictures, so perhaps we should put them in the hand of the Registrar so that they become exhibits, but perhaps Chamber exhibits. Could they be taken from the ELMO and could they be returned to the -- Mr. Groome, have the questions of the Chamber triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd like to ask one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One question. I tried my utmost best to have everything perfectly ready for putting the questions to the witness. Unfortunately, it was not. One question, and I'm apologising to those assisting us. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: General Smith, my question, only if you know, in a low trajectory shot of a mortar, is the angle of ascent always the same as the angle of descent to the target?

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it gets steeper on the entry. On the downward track. A greater amount of gravity is involved than charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have two follow-up questions on that. Further questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do the tables consider both the angle of firing and the angle of descent so that you know exactly how much steeper it lands than it has been fired to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they do, but I'm -- it's been a long time since I looked at tables.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then the second question is does the elevation from where a shell is fired have may have an impact there as well so as to say that if you fire from a higher position landing at a lower position, that even the angle of descent will be more different from the angle of firing?

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would probably mathematically anyhow, it would affect it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just want to use the opportunity with your leave to have at least two minutes from this audio that was requested by our client so the general can recognise whether it was the voice of General Mladic or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One minute should be sufficient --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to give an opportunity to Mr. Smith to see whether he recognises the voice of Mr. Mladic and his own voice I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can in a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] The general assumes that you have already heard about the incident in Sarajevo this morning. "I heard about it five minutes ago, but I don't know for certain what it is about. "Well --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's it. If we want the witness to recognise the voice of Mr. Mladic, everyone should switch to channel 6. Could the witness be assisted in moving to channel 6. And then we play 30 seconds. We do not need translation at this moment, I would say, because it's recognition of a voice. Could you restart the portion you would like to play.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This should be enough to -- Do you recognise the voice, Mr. Smith, you heard on channel 6?

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. One minute. I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are now back on 4. Did you recognise the voice as the person with whom you spoke at the time.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not clearly, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not clearly.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the interpreter's voice more clearly, but I think that's just the quality of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- recording and that I am going deaf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's. Mr. Lukic, if you want to consult for a second you can do that because we're at the very end of the testimony of this witness, but please do it quickly. And not -- at a low voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, low voice. Low voice, I said. Mr. -- Mr. -- Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We cannot ask for more from this witness. If he can recognise the voice of Mr. Mladic that would be fine, but if he doesn't. And if he can explain who is the translator, if he recognises the translator's voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who was the translator? Was it your translator or was it --

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I could hear was known as Darko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And he was translating on your behalf.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was your translator you say.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would expect him to be involved in a telephone conversation you would have with a B/C/S-speaking person.

utterances.speaker: RUPERT SMITH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further questions? Then, Mr. Smith, this concludes, although a little bit in a chaotic way, your testimony. I would have to instruct you again that you should not communicate with anyone, whether Prosecution, Defence, or whomever apart from those we permitted you to speak with about your testimony because we cannot exclude under all circumstances that there will not be a continuation. I leave it to that at this moment. But I already would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the only thing you are expected to do is to check anything which is so urgent that we could not deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please assign numbers to the two sketches used during the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit C2, and Exhibit C3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they are both in evidence. If there's nothing else, we adjourn for the day. I would like to apologise again to the -- all those assisting us. I -- before adjourning, I also put on the record that this Chamber will not sit in the week of the 11th of March and also not in the week of the 18th of March in response to a request by the Defence. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, the 29th of January, at 9.30 in the morning -- it will be at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.31 p.m.,
